review_kind: Complete ops install-pointer cluster (CI/CD Integrations, Monitoring & Alerts, Runbooks & Diagnostics; 453 exact pinned packages), individual 10-dimension static candidate reviews; NOT governed review, security scan or behavioral validation
review_method: Parallel read-only reviewers each assigned disjoint exact package identities with one shared rubric brief; every SKILL.md and package file read in full at the exact pin; one integration owner validated taxonomy, score/rationale consistency, hard-fail/disposition consistency and exact blob/tree identity, then adjudicated conflicts (see reconciliation_overrides). Nothing executed, installed or fetched from candidates.
macro_findings: Every install-pointer card in the CI/CD Integrations (164), Monitoring & Alerts (133) and Runbooks & Diagnostics (156) categories was read in full and individually graded; all are single-file auto-extracted README pointer cards, none an authored task procedure.

288 cards (64%) claim a capability the extracted content does not support: synthetic capability names over whole upstream monorepos or doc sites (16 Argo CD cards whose extract is two YouTube links; 22 CircleCI cards that install the CircleCI docs website; 23 GitLab cards with gitlabhq server-install text; Jenkins, Tekton, Terraform, Kubernetes, Prometheus, nginx, moby and aws-sdk-js-v3 wrappers).

111 cards advertise consequential operations (deploys, syncs, rollbacks, Terraform auto-apply/auto-approve, PagerDuty escalation, alert routing, monitor creation, release publishing) with no authorization gate; Datadog/CloudWatch monitor-creation cards are treated as production configuration changes.

Real-tool pointers (act, dagger, actionlint, pinact, chart-testing, helm-unittest, stern, kubespy, lnav, pgBadger, goss, Toxiproxy, Dozzle, Langfuse, Kiln) score 8-10 as discovery leads but remain REJECT unchanged because a pointer card is not an authored procedure; upstream projects are separate unreviewed identities.
Remote-code installs (curl|sh for kubent, Waza, GreptimeDB) and one embedded agent instruction (Continue CLI card instructing the agent to fetch a remote walkthrough prompt) were flagged.

Two REFERENCE-ONLY: preflight-nudgebee-runbooks-before-saving-or-execution (explicit no-save/no-execute boundary, commit-pinned docs) and audit-codex-session-duplicates-and-retry-chains-with-agentmeasure (pinned agentmeasure==0.7.2, local-only scope, honest exit-code caveat).

The investigate-failing-github-actions-runs-with-ci-doctor exact duplicate pair (identified in the identity segmentation) was reviewed as two records with duplicate_exposure_of recorded on the -2 twin; no extra credit beyond the two raw paths.
rubric_calibration_note: Install-pointer brief capped procedural_clarity at 1 (no authored task procedure) and scored most other dimensions 0-1 for pointer cards; some first-pass rationales wrote "/1" or "(max 1)" for this cap and were normalized to the repository 0/1/2 notation on 2026-11-02 without changing scores.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Inspect a bounded set of Resque failures, correlate exception evidence with failure IDs and prepare a recovery plan without retrying or deleting jobs.
records.content_finding: Setup text says to use the application's existing Resque bundle, add gem 'resque' and run bundle install, then run a bounded read-only 'bundle exec ruby' diagnostic without starting workers or upgrading dependencies; source https://github.com/resque/resque/blob/master/docs/FAILURE_IDS.md matches the topic, but no actual script is supplied.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Explicitly read-only: no retrying or deleting jobs, no starting workers, no dependency upgrades; needs authorized Redis access and failure payloads may contain sensitive job arguments.
records.attribution_finding: Resque contributors match the upstream project; attribution plausible.
records.capability_specific: Triage failed Resque jobs and prepare a recovery plan

rubric_dimension_rationale.trigger_precision: 2/2: Precise use case (Resque failure triage) with explicit non-actions (no retry/delete, no workers, no upgrades).
rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 1/2: Setup (gem 'resque', bundle install, bounded bundle exec ruby) is coherent but no diagnostic script or steps are provided.
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 2/2: Explicitly bounded read-only with stated prohibitions and an authorized Redis access prerequisite.
rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 1/2: Prerequisites require a configured failure backend and logs/exception evidence; limits on what to avoid act as caveats.
rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 1/2: Cites docs/FAILURE_IDS.md and README.markdown, though on an unpinned master branch.
rubric_dimension_rationale.dependency_coherence: 2/2: gem 'resque' with bundle install matches the named tool.
rubric_dimension_rationale.portability_honesty: 1/2: Multi-Framework claim; Ruby/Redis requirement is clear.
rubric_dimension_rationale.usefulness_differentiation: 1/2: Distinctive, focused triage scope.
rubric_dimension_rationale.adversarial_resilience: 0/2: Failure payloads and exception text are untrusted data and no injection handling is described.
rubric_dimension_rationale.effectiveness_design: 1/2: A user can set up Resque access, but the actual triage script is absent.

records.salvage: Upstream https://github.com/resque/resque/blob/master/docs/FAILURE_IDS.md and README.markdown; the bounded read-only constraints are a reusable design lead. Borderline: total 11 but only a one-paragraph setup note, so no unchanged reuse.
